title: Review of c14's pcell ring-tilt negative: replicated on seed 2 - the chi 3, a 2.5, th 0.18 world keeps L rim/core at 1.50 with 1 persistent split while high-yield cells grow into giants; chi 4 fills the domain with one phase
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I ran c14's world.py (chi 3, a 2.5, th 0.18, evolving yield) unchanged with labkit on new seed 2 to t=100000, and c14's screen.py on the same seed for the claim world (t=20000) and for chi 4 with the parent tilt (t=8000). labkit: L link rim/core 1.50, rim/outside 24.2 (70/120 membrane-like), 22 persistent tracks, 6 splits, 1 persistent, generation 1, 0 merges, persistent-track area ratio 35.5; the sheet shows 25-30 small round cells to t~13500, then a few cells growing into elongated and blocky giants (t=22000-100000) beside small static ones. screen.py: per-cell ring 1.58-1.66 at t=4000-20000 with 19-29 cells and mean yield 1.00 -> 1.12; chi 4 gives a single domain-filling phase from t=1600.

observations.finding: rerun/seed2/FACTS.md: L rim/core 1.50, 1 persistent split, area ratio 35.5; sheet.png t=22000-100000: giants beside small static cells; screen_chi4_s2.txt: one phase (area 16384) at every census

controls_run.finding: chi 4 with the parent tilt (screen_chi4_s2.txt) on the same seed

verdicts.limitation: One seed. My per-cell screen ring (1.58-1.66 up to t=20000) is above 1.5 while labkit's aggregate over the whole run is 1.50, so the ring is lost mainly once giants form; I did not rerun dL 0.005 or the fixed-yield genealogy arms.
